# updateinfo fixtures

Everything here is regenerated by `./generate.sh` (`OFFLINE=1` skips the
download and the container steps). Tools used: createrepo_c and modifyrepo_c
1.2.6 with its python binding, dnf5 5.4.7.0 (in the `localhost/s3tools` image,
Fedora 45), zstd.

| File | What it is | How it was made |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `real/rocky9-baseos.xml` | RLBA-2022:7404 and RLSA-2022:6602 | updateinfo.xml of `https://dl.rockylinux.org/pub/rocky/9/BaseOS/x86_64/os`, two advisories kept byte for byte by `trim.go` |
| `real/rocky8-appstream.xml` | RLSA-2019:2512 and RLBA-2019:3522, with module collections | the same for `rocky/8/AppStream/x86_64/os` |
| `real/fedora43-updates.xml` | FEDORA-2026-727b73bfa0, FEDORA-2025-5efdb69e46, FEDORA-2026-eb2fc8e93d, with reboot and relogin flags | the same for `fedora/linux/updates/43/Everything/x86_64` (zstd compressed on the mirror); written by createrepo_c, so rewriting it must give the same bytes |
| `model.xml` | four advisories with every field the model has | `ground_truth.py`: createrepo_c's `xml_dump_updaterecord` and `UpdateInfoXmlFile`. `updateinfo_test.go` builds the same advisories in Go and compares the output byte for byte |
| `dnf.xml` | three advisories for packages that every Fedora image has installed (bash, coreutils, filesystem at epoch 99) | `ground_truth.py` |
| `repo/` | repomd.xml, primary, filelists, other and updateinfo of a repository | `createrepo_c --simple-md-filenames` on `rpm/testdata/hello.rpm`, then `modifyrepo_c --mdtype updateinfo dnf.xml repo/repodata` |
| `dnf-updateinfo-list.txt`, `dnf-updateinfo-info.txt`, `dnf-version.txt` | what dnf5 prints for `repo/` | `podman run --rm --network=none -v repo:/repo:ro localhost/s3tools:latest dnf5 -q -y --setopt=cachedir=/tmp/c --repofrompath=t,file:///repo --repo=t --no-gpgchecks updateinfo list --available` (and `info`) |

dnf5 lists the advisories that concern a newer version of an installed
package, hence the epoch 99 packages of `dnf.xml`.

Rewriting a complete Fedora 43 updateinfo.xml (4532 advisories, 62 MB) gives
the same bytes except where a reference has an empty title: createrepo_c writes
`title=""` for an empty string and no attribute for a missing one, the model
has one value for both and leaves the attribute out.

The Rocky Linux advisory texts are derived from Red Hat advisories under CC BY
4.0 (see the `rights` element of each); the Fedora ones are the public Bodhi
advisories.

The proofs the tests make with these files:

- `TestWriteUpdateinfoMatchesCreaterepo`, `TestDnfAdvisoriesMatchCreaterepo`:
  the writer's bytes equal createrepo_c's. `TestWriteUpdateinfoLiveCreaterepo`
  repeats it with the installed python binding.
- `TestRealAdvisories`: the real advisories are read, and written and read
  again without a change; the Fedora document is rewritten byte for byte.
- `TestCommittedRepo`: the `updateinfo` entry that modifyrepo_c registered in
  `repo/repodata/repomd.xml` is found by `ParseRepomd`, its checksums hold and
  its content is read.
- `TestModifyrepoAcceptsUpdateinfo`: `modifyrepo_c --mdtype updateinfo`
  accepts a document this package wrote and `createrepo_c --update` keeps it.
- `TestDnfListsAdvisories`: a repository whose `repomd.xml` this package wrote
  (updateinfo compressed with gzip, zstd and xz) is served to dnf5 in the
  container; its `updateinfo list` and `updateinfo info` equal the committed
  output for the createrepo_c repository.
